episode_direction.opening_activity: boring a pilot hole into a wooden display base with an old hand-cranked geared drill, then stopping when its exposed interlocking gears bind mid-turn
episode_direction.opening_location: quiet maritime museum exhibit-preparation room beside an unfinished shipwreck display
episode_direction.opening_environment: a practical museum prep space with timber mounts, conservation crates, muted work lamps, and nautical artifacts waiting to be installed
episode_direction.topic_visual_link: The visibly jammed hand-powered gear train echoes the Antikythera mechanism's tightly packed gears and immediately raises the idea that sophisticated mechanical computation can exist without electricity.
episode_direction.opening_visual_proof: In the first seconds, the crone's hand turns the drill crank while two exposed metal gears rotate together, catch abruptly tooth-to-tooth, and freeze the drill bit above the wood.
episode_direction.curiosity_trigger: the crank suddenly resists with a dry metallic click while the meshed gears remain visibly locked
episode_direction.trigger_object: the exposed gear pair of the hand-cranked drill
episode_direction.reaction: She narrows her large eyes at the frozen gears, gives the raven a knowing sideways glance, and tests the crank once more with one long finger.
episode_direction.entry_retrieval: She releases the drill, follows the line of its meshed gears with one pointed finger, then reaches beneath a folded protective cloth on the same work surface and reveals her glass orb; her moss-green sleeve and long fingers remain clearly in frame as she turns it toward the camera.
episode_direction.world_style_hint: submerged Mediterranean archaeology shifting into precise bronze mechanical cutaways, engraved astronomical dials, and luminous orbital geometry
episode_direction.reason: A hand-cranked drill gives the crone a compact, believable task whose suddenly jammed visible gears naturally mirror the ancient mechanism's defining combination of manual power, dense gearing, and unexpected sophistication.

body: In 1900, sponge divers found a wreck off Antikythera.
Its cargo included a corroded bronze lump.
Inside were tightly packed, precision-cut gears.
The mechanism was built over two thousand years ago.
A hand crank moved pointers across astronomical dials.
One dial tracked the Sun and Moon.
Others modeled cycles used to predict eclipses.
Another tracked the cycle of major Greek games.
Inscriptions even explained parts of its operation.
script_plan.optional_closing: It was a hand-powered mechanical model of the heavens.
